title: Talking About the Past: Past Continuous
summary: Learn how to talk about actions that were happening at a specific time in the past. This helps you tell better stories about your day.

sections.p: We use the past continuous to talk about an action that was in progress at a specific time in the past. To make this tense, we use the past form of the verb 'to be' (was or were) plus the main verb with '-ing' at the end. Use 'was' with I, he, she, and it. Use 'were' with you, we, and they.

ex.en: I was sleeping at 10 PM last night.
ex.mean: At 10 PM last night, my action of sleeping was in progress.

ex.en: They were watching a movie at that time.
ex.mean: At that moment in the past, they were in the middle of watching a movie.

sections.p: To ask a question in the past continuous, we change the order of the words. We put 'Was' or 'Were' first, then the subject (like you or he), and then the verb with '-ing'. This is very useful when you want to ask what someone was doing yesterday.

ex.en: What were you doing at 8 o'clock?
ex.mean: I want to know your action at that past time.
Did she have the action of working late happening yesterday?

sections.p: To say what you were NOT doing in the past, just add 'not' after 'was' or 'were'. You can also use the short forms 'wasn't' or 'weren't'. This helps you correct mistakes or explain your past actions clearly.

ex.en: I was not listening to music.
ex.mean: My action at that time did not include listening to music.
They were not looking or listening at that moment.

tip: Always remember the two parts: was/were + verb-ing. Think of 'was/were' as the helper and '-ing' as the engine of the action!

quiz.en: I ___ reading a book when you called.
She wasn't ___ TV; she was studying.
___ it raining when you went outside?
We ___ sleeping when the phone rang.
